assessment: This article is of particular interest to researchers in the fields of neuroecology of insect olfaction and of insect–plant interactions in general. The authors investigate the olfactory signals that guide the specialist hawkmoth Manduca sexta towards plants that are used for oviposition and for nectar-feeding in a natural setting. How insects distinguish useful information from irrelevant information is an important question. The authors use elegant chemical ecology techniques and recordings of neuronal activity to ask how female moths (M. sexta) could discriminate co-occurring behaviorally relevant versus irrelevant plant and floral volatiles.
